attribution_limitations: Source conflict: the text says the patient remained free from disease flare-ups throughout the six-month follow-up, while the same paragraph and the abstract report a flare-up (recurrence) in the sixth month of follow-up. The Figure 1D caption places the flare-up after 6 months and Figure 2 labels the last time point "after Month 6". Both text sides are review_only; the caption flare-up is kept as its own caption-governed fact.

The text reports improvement within 1 day after the initial treatment and cites Figure 1B, while the Figure 1B caption dates the improvement at Day 2 after treatment; the source does not state its day-numbering convention.
The PGA, IGA, scaling and erythema scores at baseline, Day 2, Month 6 and after Month 6 are given only inside the Figure 2 image; the text describes the scales but prints no score values.

The first treatment is labelled in the source as "ASCE + Skin Rejuvenation Lyophilized Vial (SRLV)‐S", while the text and abstract describe rose stem cell-derived exosomes (RSCEs); the discussion defines ASCEs as exosomes from human adipose tissue-derived mesenchymal stem cells.
The case text says the patient "presented with a severe recurrent SD during his teenage years" and does not state when the patient presented for the treatment described, or his age at disease onset.

evidence.quote: we prescribed the patient a regimen of post‐procedural treatment for maintenance to prevent flare‐ups of the disease, which included the application of a twice‐daily topical moisturizer with exosomes (Exobalm, ExoCoBio Inc., Seoul, Republic of Korea) to the entire face for 21 days, followed by nightly application for 1 month, and then maintenance with twice‐weekly application for an additional month.

A flare-up was present before treatment.
